audit_headline: Jimmy Lock & Key has no website linked on its Google Business Profile, which means potential customers searching online cannot learn more, see services, or find a second way to contact the business.
summary: Jimmy Lock & Key operates in Wauseon, OH with a strong 4.9-star rating from 17 reviews and a primary category of Locksmith. The profile lists hours and a phone number, but has no website linked and only 1 photo visible. The most recent review is from 8 months ago, and the recent reviews highlight responsiveness and car key expertise.

sections.title: Google Business Profile
sections.summary: The profile has the essentials—phone number, hours, and the correct Locksmith category—but lacks a website link and has minimal visual content with only 1 photo visible.

findings.observation: No website is linked on the Google Business Profile, so searchers cannot learn about services, pricing, service area, or find additional contact options beyond the phone number.
findings.recommendation: Add a website to the profile. If you don't have one, create a simple one-page site with your services, service area, contact info, and hours, or use a free Google Site or Facebook Business Page as an interim step.

findings.observation: Only 1 photo is visible on the profile, which provides almost no visual context about the business, the owner, work examples, or service vehicles.
findings.recommendation: Upload 10-15 photos showing your service vehicle with branding, you at work, examples of locksmith jobs (car keys, rekeyed locks, etc.), and your service area. Update photos every few months.

findings.observation: The profile lists hours as 3:00 PM – 12:00 AM on Monday, then complex split hours Tuesday-Friday (12:00 AM – 12:00 PM, 3:00 PM – 12:00 AM), and 24 hours Saturday-Sunday. This creates a 3-hour gap (12:00 PM – 3:00 PM) on weekdays, which may turn away callers during midday emergencies.
findings.recommendation: If you are available during the 12:00 PM – 3:00 PM window on weekdays, update your hours to reflect that. If not, consider adding a note in your business description about emergency availability or callback options during closed hours.

findings.observation: The primary category is correctly set to Locksmith, which matches the business name and the services described in reviews.

sections.title: Reviews & Reputation
sections.summary: The 4.9-star rating from 17 reviews is strong, but the most recent review is from 8 months ago, and review velocity has slowed significantly compared to the cluster of reviews from 3-4 years ago.

findings.observation: The 4.9-star rating from 17 reviews is excellent and well above the threshold where most customers trust a local service business.

The most recent review is from 8 months ago, and before that the next four reviews are all from 3-4 years ago, indicating a significant drop in review activity. Fresh reviews are a recognized relevance and trust signal.
findings.recommendation: After every completed job, ask satisfied customers to leave a Google review. Send a follow-up text or email with a direct link to your review page (find it in your Google Business Profile under 'Get more reviews').

findings.observation: Three of the five recent reviews specifically mention responsiveness ('less than 30 minutes,' 'went above and beyond,' 'worked relentlessly'), and two highlight car key expertise, which are strong service differentiators.
The Google Places API does not reveal whether you have responded to reviews. Responding to reviews—especially the one 4-star review—shows engagement and can improve trust.
findings.recommendation: Log into your Google Business Profile and check if you have replied to all reviews. If not, reply to each one with a brief thank-you or acknowledgment, especially the 4-star review from betty romero.

sections.title: Website & Online Presence
sections.summary: No website is linked on the Google Business Profile, which means this audit could not evaluate whether the business has a site, and searchers have no way to learn more online.

findings.observation: No website is linked on the Google Business Profile, so potential customers cannot view services, service area, pricing guidance, or find a second contact method (like a contact form or email).
findings.recommendation: Create and link a website. At minimum, include: business name, phone number with click-to-call, services offered (car lockouts, rekeying, key duplication, etc.), service area (Wauseon and surrounding towns), and hours. Use a simple platform like Google Sites, Wix, or WordPress.

findings.observation: Because no website is linked, this audit could not check for local-search signals like a homepage title that includes 'Locksmith' and 'Wauseon,' HTTPS, mobile optimization, click-to-call links, or LocalBusiness structured data.
findings.recommendation: Once you have a website, ensure the homepage <title> tag includes 'Locksmith' and 'Wauseon, OH,' the site uses HTTPS, the phone number is a clickable tel: link, and the site is mobile-friendly. Consider adding LocalBusiness schema markup.

sections.title: Call Handling & Contact Paths
sections.summary: A phone number is listed on the profile, but the weekday midday gap in hours and the lack of a website mean some callers may not reach you or find an alternative contact method.

findings.observation: The profile lists a phone number, (419) 784-6846, which is essential for a locksmith business where most customers call during emergencies.
The hours show a 3-hour gap (12:00 PM – 3:00 PM) on weekdays, and with no website or contact form, a caller during that window has no way to leave a message or request a callback online.
findings.recommendation: Set up a missed-call text-back service or voicemail-to-text so you can respond quickly to calls that come in during closed hours. Test this by calling your own number during the midday gap and after midnight on a weekday to confirm callers can leave a message.

fix_list.action: Add a website to your Google Business Profile
fix_list.rationale: No website is linked, which means searchers cannot learn about your services, service area, or find a second way to contact you. A website is a recognized trust and relevance signal.
fix_list.where: Create a simple site (Google Sites, Wix, or WordPress), then add the URL in Google Business Profile -> Edit profile -> Website

fix_list.action: Upload 10-15 photos to your Google Business Profile
fix_list.rationale: Only 1 photo is visible, which provides almost no visual context. Photos of your service vehicle, you at work, and completed jobs help build trust and engagement.
fix_list.where: Google Business Profile -> Photos -> Add photos

fix_list.action: Ask every satisfied customer for a Google review
fix_list.rationale: Your most recent review is from 8 months ago, and fresh reviews are a recognized trust and relevance signal. Your 4.9-star rating is strong, but review velocity has slowed.
fix_list.where: After each job, send a text or email with your Google review link (find it in Google Business Profile -> Home -> Get more reviews)

fix_list.action: Update your weekday hours to eliminate the 12:00 PM – 3:00 PM gap, or add a note about midday availability
fix_list.rationale: The current hours show a 3-hour midday gap on weekdays, which may turn away emergency callers. If you are available during that window, the hours should reflect it.
fix_list.where: Google Business Profile -> Edit profile -> Hours, or add a note in the business description

fix_list.action: Reply to all reviews, especially the one 4-star review
fix_list.rationale: Responding to reviews shows engagement and can improve trust. The API does not reveal if you have replied, so this is a verify-and-do step.
fix_list.where: Google Business Profile -> Reviews -> Reply to each review

fix_list.action: Set up a missed-call text-back or voicemail-to-text service
fix_list.rationale: With no website and a midday gap in hours, callers during closed times have no way to leave a message or request a callback. Quick response to missed calls is critical for emergency locksmith work.
fix_list.where: Use a service like Google Voice, Nextiva, or your carrier's voicemail-to-text feature

fix_list.action: Once you have a website, ensure the homepage title includes 'Locksmith' and 'Wauseon, OH'
fix_list.rationale: A homepage title that includes your trade and city is a recognized local-search relevance signal. This audit could not check it because no website is linked.
fix_list.where: In your website builder, edit the homepage <title> tag (often under SEO settings or page settings)

fix_list.action: Add click-to-call phone links and LocalBusiness structured data to your website
fix_list.rationale: Click-to-call (tel: links) makes it easy for mobile visitors to call you, and LocalBusiness schema helps search engines understand your business details. This is a verify-and-do step once you have a site.
fix_list.where: In your website code or builder, wrap your phone number in <a href='tel:+14197846846'>, and add LocalBusiness JSON-LD schema to the homepage

not_checked: Whether you have responded to your 17 reviews — the Google Places API does not reveal this. Log into your Google Business Profile and check the Reviews section to confirm.

Whether you have a website at all, and if so, whether it uses HTTPS, is mobile-friendly, has a homepage title with 'Locksmith' and 'Wauseon,' or includes LocalBusiness structured data — no website is linked on the profile, so this audit could not read one.

Your actual call answer rate or missed-call volume — this data is not available in the Google Business Profile. Call your own number during closed hours and after midnight on a weekday to test your voicemail setup.

Whether your service area extends beyond Wauseon — the profile lists a street address and is not marked as a service-area business. If you serve surrounding towns, consider adding a service-area list to your business description or website.
closing_note: Jimmy Lock & Key has a strong reputation and the right category, but the lack of a website and minimal photos are significant gaps that limit your visibility and trust signals. The fixes above are ranked by impact and effort — start with the website and photos, then build momentum with fresh reviews and better call handling.
